note: Sources: her quantization lecture is the recording transcribed in course/L13.transcript.md (it opens "for this lecture, we will cover large language model quantizations"); course/L12.transcript.md is the serving lecture, and the slide markers in both transcripts point at the other PDF. Slides: course/L12.txt / L12.pdf.
beats: Hook: squeeze 0, 0.8, 1.2 and 2.5 into 4-bit integers. What comes back out? (0, 0.714, 1.071, 2.5: recompute) Four bowls of flour and one scoop (line_quant_scoop_bowls).

Symmetric round-to-nearest (slide 9): choose one scoop size so the biggest amount is exactly seven scoops, S = 2.5 / 7 = 0.357; every amount becomes a whole number of scoops: 0, 2, 3, 7 (red pen on a code-drawn ruler of 15 ticks).

Dequantize: scoops x scoop size; whatever was levelled off is the rounding error (line_quant_scoop_level). Use [-7, 7], not [-8, 7], so zero sits in the middle (line_bits_hook_rails from L12-01's plan).

Asymmetric (slide 11): a lopsided range also gets a zero point, like re-zeroing a kitchen scale under the bowl (line_quant_tare_scale); old days: weights symmetric, activations asymmetric; today: symmetric plus fine-grained groups.

Granularity (slide 10): one scoop for the whole pantry is sized by the biggest sack, and the spices round to nothing (line_quant_giant_scoop); one scoop per shelf fits each row (line_quant_shelf_scoops); per-row error 2.08 vs per-tensor 2.28 (recompute).

Which axis (slide 12): group along the input features, the axis the multiply adds up; weights are measured offline in groups of 128 (line_quant_night_prep), activations per token on the fly as they arrive (line_quant_conveyor_scoop).

Pitfall, does it save compute? (slides 13-14): only if the GPU can multiply in the small format; otherwise every weight is unpacked back to FP16 first, and unpacking eight INT4 from one 32-bit word into half2 is fiddly (line_quant_vacuum_unpack).
Benefits (slide 16): less memory, a big model on fewer GPUs (line_quant_van_fit); less traffic, faster small-batch decoding (line_tap_glass); simpler math.

Slide 17: W4A16 vs W8A8 vs W4A4: memory and small batches favour 4-bit weights; at large batches the winner is whatever the GPU multiplies natively: A100 FP16, H100 FP8, B100 FP4 (line_quant_plug_adapter, taped slide 17).
Takeaway: quantization is three choices: the levels, who shares a scale, and whether the hardware speaks the format; next: making 4-bit weights accurate (GPTQ, AWQ).
Cover (line_cover_l12_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the cook holds one measuring scoop above four bowls of flour, from empty to a big heap.
